blocks.x: Support copilot with harness-gated rollout, 42% deflection on tier-1 volume and CSAT up while handle time falls 38%

Identity withheld, a SaaS vendor whose support docs had grown faster than its search and whose tier-1 agents answered the same nine questions daily. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline fortnight measured the nine questions: 63% of tier-1 tickets matched nine documented issues, agents composing answers the docs already contained, and an earlier chatbot retired after hallucinating a configuration flag that never existed.
Deflection was the goal everyone claimed and nobody measured honestly. Without an evaluation baseline, every proposal was a belief system.

We built the copilot behind an evaluation harness: retrieval over versioned docs with product-version awareness, generated answers grounded with citations to the exact doc section and gated against the labeled-ticket baseline, escalation paths that hand the human the draft instead of making them start over, and weekly quality reviews where support leads read sampled answers in the open. Deflection became a measured, honest number.
